cards.text: Jesus, God's Son, is with His disciples, His closest followers. They come to Him and ask, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” Friend, that's like standing up in the middle of the staff meeting and asking, “So who's getting the corner office?”

cards.question: The disciples want to know who's the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. What does Jesus do first?

answers.text: He invites a little child to stand among them
He sends them up the mountain to pray
He writes in the dirt with His finger

cards.question: With a little child standing among them, Jesus says unless you change and become like little ___, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
So who does Jesus say is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?

answers.text: Whoever humbles himself like this little child
Whoever gives the most away to the poor
Whoever has followed Him the longest

cards.question: Jesus says whoever welcomes a little child like this in His name welcomes Jesus Himself.

cards.text: Then Jesus gets serious: if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Him to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the depths of the sea. A MILLSTONE, friend, not a pebble and not a paperweight.

cards.question: Jesus says woe to the world for the causes of sin, and these stumbling blocks must come. But who else does He say woe to?

answers.text: The man through whom they come
The one who trips over them
The ones who never warned others

cards.text: Then Jesus says if your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. Friend, my mustache is the only pair of hands I've got, and I just heard that and tucked it behind my apron.

cards.question: Jesus says it's better to keep both hands and both feet, even if it means being thrown into the eternal fire.
Jesus says the same about another part of the body. If your ___ causes you to sin, it's better to enter life with just one than to have two and be thrown into the fire of hell.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “See that you do not look down on any of these little ones.” Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for years, and EVERY person who opened it looked down on me, and I mean LITERALLY.

cards.question: Jesus says not to look down on any of these little ones. What reason does He give?

answers.text: Their angels in heaven always see His Father's face
They will inherit the whole earth one day
Their names are written in the book of life

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “What do you think?” A man has a hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray.

cards.question: One sheep out of a hundred goes astray. What does Jesus say the man will do?

answers.text: Leave the ninety-nine and search for the lost one
Stay with the ninety-nine and wait for it to return
Send his servants out to bring it home

cards.text: And if he finds it, way out on those hills? One little sheep, out of a hundred.

cards.question: Jesus says if the man finds the lost sheep, he rejoices over it just the same as over the ninety-nine.
Jesus ties the story of the lost sheep to the Father in heaven. What does He say about the Father?

answers.text: He is not willing that any little one should perish
He keeps only the ones who never wander off
He waits for the lost to find their own way back

cards.text: Now Jesus gets practical. If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately, and friend, privately means NOT the group chat and NOT a reply-all to the whole office.

cards.question: You go to your brother privately, and he listens to you. What does Jesus say you've done?

answers.text: You have won your brother over
You have proved that you were right
You have kept the matter quiet

cards.question: But what if your brother won't listen when you go to him privately? What does Jesus say to do next?

answers.text: Take one or two others along
Let it drop and move on

cards.question: Jesus says to take others along so that every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three ___.

cards.text: I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries who swore they still had a charge, so friend, I LOVE a two or three witness rule. But what if your brother refuses to listen even to them?

cards.question: Your brother refuses to listen to the one or two others. Who does Jesus say to tell next?
Jesus says if your brother refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.” Friend, that's the kind of line you read TWICE, so go ahead, I'll wait.

cards.question: Jesus says if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you. Who does He say will do it?
Jesus says where two or three gather together in His name, ___ is there with them.

cards.text: Hold that thought, friend. Jesus has a whole lot more to say, and we're not done listening.
